source_snapshot.criteria: Configured address is correct and LED on; ping succeeds; after cable removal addresses are disabled and LED off.

original_test_intent: Verify a dedicated Mellanox port accepts the approved IPv4 configuration, reaches its peer, visibly indicates link, loses carrier/reachability and LED when unplugged, then safely restores its approved state.
original_method: Apply a conflict-free temporary IPv4 configuration on an isolated port, record bounded peer traffic and link/LED evidence, have an operator remove and reconnect the exact cable, observe down/recovery behavior, then restore the baseline configuration.
manual_activity: Engineer resolves address-disabled semantics and approves the isolated IP plan; operator removes/reconnects the mapped cable and captures LED evidence; agent performs only approved configuration and bounded checks.
required_inputs: Conflict-free IPv4 address/prefix/route and peer with duplicate-address check
Definition of address-disabled after carrier loss: assignment removal, operational unusability, or carrier/reachability only
Vendor LED on/off legend and qualified operator
Independent OOB/console, baseline restore, recovery and invalid-run policy
safety_requirements: Never modify the management/BMC or shared production interface
Verify address uniqueness, routes, bonds/bridges/VLANs and rollback before applying
Use bounded ping and stop on duplicate IP, route drift, access loss, wrong cable or failed reconnect
Preserve full logs and operator evidence; do not clear logs
Restore the approved address/routes/cable state without automatic reboot or retry
agent_execution_scope: Collect baseline addresses/routes/link/counters and validate approved plan
Apply temporary IPv4 and bounded peer checks on the named interface
Record carrier and reachability through operator disconnect/reconnect and restore baseline
Do not decide ambiguous acceptance, handle cables, modify management, retry automatically or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Define cable-loss address semantics and LED acceptance
Review complete electronic/physical evidence and issue PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Only partially applicable; it applies IPv4 but omits address conflict/DAD-equivalent checks, bounded ping, physical cable/LED states, reconnect recovery and cleanup, and uses unsafe SSH.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use secure managed access to apply the approved temporary IPv4 configuration, preserve complete address/route/link/counter state, run bounded peer ping through operator disconnect/reconnect, then restore baseline.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: IPv4 setup, correct address, LED-on, successful ping, cable removal, address/LED-down observation and 10/10 timing fields are preserved pending semantics.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a reversible dedicated-port IPv4 lifecycle with time-correlated carrier, reachability and physical LED evidence across cable removal and restoration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds conflict avoidance, exact mapping, bounded probes, reconnect and rollback while isolating the unresolved criterion.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No original electronic or physical checkpoint is discarded; ambiguous wording remains pending.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Linux commonly retains a static IPv4 address when carrier drops; interpreting 'disabled' as address deletion would require an explicit policy or network manager action.

project_override_considerations: Engineering may define disabled as carrier-down/unreachable rather than configuration removal, but that decision must be explicit and applied consistently.
expected_evidence: Configured-state correct IPv4, route, bounded ping and LED-on evidence
Cable-removal carrier, reachability, address behavior and LED-off timestamps/photos
Reconnect recovery and complete system/SEL logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The criterion says IPv4 addresses should be disabled after cable removal without defining whether assignment disappears or only carrier/reachability becomes unavailable; these are materially different behaviors.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; engineering can decide the acceptance semantics later without blocking the remaining review.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row66 Wistron-Networking-00049-V003: define whether 'IP addresses should be disable' after cable removal means the static IPv4 assignment must disappear, the interface must become operationally down, or only carrier and peer reachability must fail; provide exact NIC/physical-port/netdev, IPv4/prefix/route/peer, duplicate-address policy, expected LED mapping, cable reconnect recovery, non-management exclusions, independent OOB/console, configuration rollback and invalid-run rules. Normal retained address assignment must not be failed or passed by assumption.

review_improvement: Makes the mixed configuration, physical and recovery test traceable while preventing an invented interpretation of cable-loss address behavior.
independent_technical_reasoning: Carrier state and IPv4 assignment are separate layers: unplugging a cable normally changes operstate and reachability but does not necessarily delete a static address. Therefore evidence must report each layer independently and engineering must define which state the ambiguous word disabled refers to.
